tests.name: Provider conversation reuse and cache-compatible requests
tests.covers: 100-turn Main conversations reuse native and API sessions across restart. Rules/model changes invalidate unsafe continuations; JSON repairs keep the original fingerprint and continue the accepted native session without resending its request, including DeepSeek's own invalid-JSON rejection; API repairs reuse the saved prefix. A deleted Claude Main transcript restarts once with the full context. Group context omits commentary and repeated preambles. Missing API history recovers before inference; Codex compaction defers instruction refresh until the live turn settles, protects chat reopening and settings invalidation, and refreshes once. Missing-thread timing stays finite. Thirty-day cleanup protects current, unrelated and section-filed transcripts and still runs on Codex 0.163 and 0.164, which report no pin flag. Cache hints, API reasoning and unknown usage preserve provider contracts. Improvement settings remain user-controlled.
tests.command: node --test tests/prompt-cache.test.cjs tests/api-agent.test.cjs tests/native-cli.test.cjs tests/claude-permissions.test.cjs tests/cursor-permissions.test.cjs tests/deepseek.test.cjs tests/reply-suggestions.test.cjs tests/core.test.cjs tests/structured-inference.test.cjs

origin.problem: Repeated instructions and fresh coordinator sessions waste context and weaken provider prefix caching.
origin.fix: Resume compatible conversations, append changes and apply endpoint-specific cache hints without claiming unreported cache hits.

tests.name: Local agent creation, concurrency and delegation
tests.covers: Main, named and delegated agents create idle persistent agents through tools, inheriting conversation permissions and rejecting inactive calls, edits and permission overrides. New and resumed Codex chats receive a session-bound MCP configuration without replacing history. Agent conversations request native subagents disabled even when untracked; resume appends current developer instructions naming the real creation tool. Only local agent tools are preapproved. Stop, delete and access-setting tools work across provider bridges with compact acknowledgements; Main is undeletable but stoppable and configurable. Idle/access guards reject privilege escalation, extra arguments, self-management and late deletion after a caller stops. Child and grandchild creation inherit all three current conversation access levels rather than profile defaults. Confirmed clear archives Main or a named conversation, creates fresh provider context without changing role/workspace/access, survives restart, rejects pending work and late state changes, and rolls back failed saves. Agent profiles save without waiting for provider startup, reuse discovery and expose startup errors. Direct foreground workers retain separate sessions and start at least five simultaneous Full-access turns in the same workspace independently of the two background slots, allow nested workspaces, retain independent message queues, stop individually, return delegated results once, preserve permissions, and fail closed on cleanup or restart. Context reads include Main, search bounded visible transcripts with hash and line provenance, exclude private reasoning and hidden metadata, require an active turn and enforce current workspace/access checks on every call. Each agent retains one conversation, legacy chats migrate without losing history, deletion protects Main and pending work, and repeated delegations return only their own results. Every provider can send exact pasted text to Main; nested task requests wait for final results, reject circular chains, preserve request budgets, and cascade Stop without restarting paused conversations. Agent-created children default to Auto; available model discovery exposes supported efforts, and explicit model/effort selection persists and reaches actual turn parameters across provider bridges without changing the parent. Invalid, disabled and unavailable selections create nothing. Jev enable/disable persists across agents, preserves keys and preferences, uses Smart while off and blocks all Jev requests without reading the key; busy agents prevent toggling. Worker result cards persist in the owner conversation before model review, survive a full queue, deduplicate retries and roll back failed saves; context reads retain reports. Busy bots persist FIFO delegationQueue assignments, preserve the active task and permission ceiling, retain accepted model choices, reject dependency cycles and overflow, and cancel queued jobs by stable IDs even after promotion. Question/answer mailboxes persist and deduplicate stable IDs, validate reply/job correlation and access, bound pending messages, service waiting owners, roll back failed saves, and yield priority to direct user follow-ups. Restart retains queued assignments as Needs review; native resume preserves trusted local receipts while rejecting provider-forged mailbox items. A cancellation intent persists before its report; even a failed report save cannot cause the cancelled queued job to execute. Ownership transfer pins stable offers, saves receiver acceptance before commit, rejects stale owner versions and permission escalation, and retries without a second worker or duplicate result. Notification failure preserves committed ownership and restart keeps receipts without replay. Immutable job ancestry preserves cancellation after transfer or parent completion. Transferred ownership does not block or contaminate an unrelated delegated assignment: its notices and reports wait while the recipient processes its own helper replies. Two FIFO background slots preserve direct foreground chat; helper waits release slots, and Stop or Quit cancels admission without provider submission. Reports behind full queues retain a durable deferred review, move once when room opens, roll back failed moves and pause after restart. Deferred helper evidence blocks premature parent completion; foreign ownership mail does not occupy its inbox. Missing owners retain pending reports. Stable assignment amendments use revision checks and durable Received receipts. Native steering marks Applied only after acknowledgment; unsupported execution stops its old subtree before replacement. Unknown steering or cleanup prevents another writer. Stop races never revive work. Earlier-revision helper results remain evidence without automatic continuation. Old approvals and helper actions are rejected after a revision. Direct Apply now consumes text/images with the revision in one save and rolls back failed saves. Interrupted active jobs remain undelivered and visible to their owner after restart; recovery classifications persist without replay. Cancelled-result summaries use read-only execution, reject new agent actions and restore the original access only on a fresh user request. Contained restart resumes never-submitted versioned assignments in FIFO order only after checking workspace, original source, result owner, permission ceilings and parent revision. Attempted, legacy, paused or incompatible jobs stay under review, and interrupted replies cannot silently resume from a late receipt. Stop intent persists before child traversal and survives a crash before child-store cancellation. A failed execution-start save preserves durable acceptance without submitting a worker or inviting a duplicate retry. Foreground and delegated execution use distinct saved controllers under one bot identity. Tests cover simultaneous chat/job execution, automatic reply admission without occupying foreground chat, registered worker restart, empty registration retry, untouched orphan history, scoped mail/context reads and cross-context receipt deduplication, and trusted job-details revisions with stable retries. A controlled host check retains its existing slot without failing queued assignments or foreground chat in another context; an ended, cancelled, mismatched or unconfirmed check still fences admission. A worker context left signed out by a transient Codex account error retries while queued work waits there, and starts that work once the account loads. Another bot's stopping check delays (does not fail) queued background work; an admission failure before checks blocks the task and frees the bot; a rejected turn start closes its budget request; a lost owner chat holds a transferred job for review instead of blocking startup, and chats owning undelivered jobs cannot be deleted. Stopping a Codex job ends the processes its turn started (a real long-lived child) while sparing the app-server and its earlier helpers, and an unreadable process list holds the cleanup and blocks new work. State snapshots carry no inline images (counts kept) and serve each one on demand. A helper's job is held while its question is queued for or being read by the recipient, then delivered after the answered follow-up, once the question was read without an answer, or when the owner cannot receive it (paused queue). Tool-result images and a pending message's images are also kept out of snapshots and served on demand. No agent can delete an agent through any provider bridge; only the user delete path removes a profile and still refuses queued or pending work. After a restart, held assignments change only by a user decision (reconcileJob): Return delivers them to their owner as interrupted, and Start reruns only never-started work that still matches its owner, permissions and workspace; work that may have run is never started again, failed saves keep the job held, and a second restart of resumed work records it as uncertain.

origin.problem: Harness could run only one active session and had no persistent agent delegation.
origin.fix: Coordinate independent controllers with concurrent execution and permission-preserving task handoffs; retain cleanup guards and targeted Stop.

tests.name: Codex agent creation reaches the sidebar
tests.covers: Installed Codex resumes an old conversation, receives explicit developer instructions, executes the real agent_create MCP against the Harness backend without another approval, persists inherited permissions and renders the new agent from the state event. Local Responses mock only; no paid inference or user data changes. The new agent_models tool dispatches through real Codex MCP before creation, and the created profile defaults to Auto.

origin.problem: A chat claimed to create an agent using the provider's native subagent tool, while no Harness profile existed; MCP discovery alone missed an execution approval block.
origin.fix: Append current Harness instructions on resume and preapprove only the permission-checked local agent tools; verify a real MCP call through the sidebar.

tests.name: Agent UI and delete dialog selection
tests.covers: Agent creation, switching, deletion through the context menu without sidebar delete buttons, compact Mosaic Main row with search and New bot above it, no bottom New agent/Edit controls, and sidebar scrolling; reopening Delete clears stale text selection. Right-click and Shift+F10 menus use Open/Edit/Delete labels with red Delete, stay within the viewport, support arrow/Escape navigation and focus restoration, target the clicked agent, and respect Main/busy protections. Slash commands /help /compact /clear /stop /agents /settings run locally without routing/model calls. Clear asks for confirmation and resets only the selected conversation; cancel retains the input. Delegate controls are absent; an agent waiting for nested tasks shows Waiting and keeps Stop targeting its conversation. All buttons and nested button labels are unselectable, including dynamic dialogs, while composer text stays selectable. Shared in-app confirmations show clear/close/startup messages, open without selecting buttons, handle Escape and repeated opens, retain drafts on cancellation and keep cursor styles visible. Typing / shows all commands, name prefixes filter case-insensitively, arrows and active-descendant track selection, Tab only completes, Enter/click dispatch locally, Escape/blur dismiss, unknown prefixes show an empty state, and the menu fits at 840x640 with 150% text. Selecting clear still confirms. Settings save each dropdown and workspace selection immediately, scoped to the selected agent. Failed saves restore saved/default values and do not block later writes. Check edits and removals autosave; incomplete check drafts survive tab changes and block Close, X and Escape until fixed or removed. API providers join the main provider list as expandable rows, preserve key drafts, and retain save/clear key and confirmed removal actions. API and Jev plug buttons toggle enabled state without expanding settings; Jev keeps its key and supports keyboard toggling. Jev appears as a collapsed provider row, expands by click or keyboard, retains key drafts across provider renders, resets on Settings reopen, and reflects configured/unavailable states. Settings About tab owns the app identity, version, diagnostics, logs and update controls; tab switching hides other panels and existing update checks still work. Offscreen screenshots use software rendering for Linux/Xvfb and Windows, with the output directory created before the first capture. All thirteen slash commands are listed. New command pickers search models, supported efforts, access modes and agents, support keyboard selection and Escape, retain target-agent drafts, persist access for agents without conversations, reject unavailable/busy changes, survive queued close events and fit large text. Context distinguishes reported usage from unsupported providers; status displays task/queue/child data safely. Export writes selected-agent Markdown via a mocked save picker, writes nothing on cancel and preserves input on write errors. Startup and UI checks have separate 30-second budgets so cold Chromium startup cannot consume the test budget; timeout errors report the active phase. Local model controls show load state and context, support load/unload and status retry, disable unloading during agent work, and hide for hosted selections. Connection progress appears in the header and provider rows, includes other agents and browser sign-in, disables duplicate connects, and clears after discovery failure or completion. A computed-style audit checks all populated text and controls at every Font Size option, including sidebar/Overview typography, command descriptions, local-model controls and the + icon; the smallest window at 150% keeps the sidebar scrollable and the heading/access controls readable. The agents divider supports pointer capture, Escape cancellation, arrow/Home/End keys and reset, persists its width across reloads, and clamps to leave conversation room while retaining the preferred width. Dialogs support corner dragging and Alt+arrow resizing with viewport limits; Settings keeps its footer visible and narrowed Overview cards reflow to one column. Minimal chat keeps Hub in a dedicated pinned tile above specialist previews, with Settings in the sidebar and advanced model/routing controls inside Options. Dark, Light and System appearance follow native palettes, persist on reload, preserve drafts, avoid provider calls, and keep explicit overrides fixed when the OS changes. No persistent text or action footer appears below the composer; Clear, Commands, context, usage and permission details remain hidden inside Options until opened, and connection progress remains in the header. Options stays open for inside controls, closes on outside clicks or Escape, restores trigger focus on Escape, and preserves active tasks and drafts without sending Stop. Background activity shows one result owner, direct Open chat and targeted Stop; reports remain visible while the owner is busy. Fake worker output verifies responsive typing, navigation, queued corrections and local Stop feedback, with separate latency measurements. Queued assignments appear with their actual owner and target Stop by assignment ID without interrupting unrelated work. Collapsed mailbox questions display sender, Received acknowledgment and escaped text; incoming messages are distinct from worker results. Separate foreground/execution snapshots retain one sidebar bot and an enabled Send. Nonmodal job details preserve the draft, render bounded literal evidence, show Received/Applied updates and dismiss on Escape/outside. Explicit background approvals defer and reply to the exact context. Send remains hit-testable at 1320px and 840px with 150% font. Background quota controls validate and save immediately, update their explanation, and show a paused job with its reported allowance reason. Composer file inputs reject binary selections atomically, preserve per-chat drafts and failed snapshots, support file-only send and history recall, and render file contents literally in collapsed details. No routine dialog, button, Repeat action or routine IPC exists. A state update keeps focus on an attachment remove button, message images load on demand. Normal bots retain completed delegated instructions and responses with a writable direct composer, including an initially empty direct chat and navigation; pending work disables typing and sub-bots remain read-only. Worker report cards show only sender, status, answer and compact controls by default; internal handoff messages stay out of the visible chat. Task details use one scrolling panel, completed tasks hide update controls, and chat has only View task with no duplicate details. Minimal task view shows the assignment and bot status without duplicated replies, ownership, revisions, access metadata, or unconfigured checks; real check failures remain visible. Buttons have no focus outlines and Enter never activates native or custom buttons or implicitly submits input forms. Confirmations, approvals, menus and the startup-error dialog never auto-select actions; mouse clicks and composer Enter still work. Shared connector Settings validates inputs, saves/connects, edits, clears secrets, disconnects/reconnects and removes connectors with a readable narrow layout. Connectors Settings automatically displays bot-written JSON additions, edits and removal; incomplete writes preserve the displayed list and the error clears on repair. Provider connection, install and refresh errors scroll into view in short Settings windows. Native text context menus copy selected reports, paste into editable fields and never enable Paste for locked fields. Mosaic uses one layout for light, dark and System; bot search reveals matching children with their creators, tile icons have visible geometry, separate Settings navigation fits at desktop and 390/600px widths, connector actions survive refresh, and chat and settings are captured for visual review. Provider plugs use vivid green and faint grey in both themes, keep their state visible while controls are locked, and leave disconnected labels readable. Task close stays visible outside native title-bar controls at 50/75/100/115/200/300% zoom before and after scrolling; the composer has no model selector. Group form fields align vertically without blue focus outlines or empty error markers. Leading @ opens current-member suggestions with case-insensitive filtering, mouse/arrow/Enter/Tab selection without sending, Escape, preserved draft suffixes and no popup in direct chats or email text. The group editor's Who replies list shows members unticked, numbers ticked rows, reorders by arrows and drag, saves replyOrder and shows it again on reopen. /clear in a group (tests/group-chat-ui-check.cjs, run by the smoke) opens the fresh group chat with an empty message box.

origin.problem: Delete dialog retained text selection between deletions.
origin.fix: Clear selection on dialog open/close and prevent selection of button labels.

tests.name: App confirmation replies and cancellation
tests.covers: Confirmation replies require a matching pending id and an explicit boolean. Window close, renderer crash and reload cancel pending operations; unavailable windows never approve.

origin.problem: Native confirmations interrupted the Harness UI and obscured the pointer.
origin.fix: Use styled in-app dialogs over a sender-validated request/reply bridge; cancel requests when their window disappears.

tests.name: Conversation export and compaction records
tests.covers: Markdown export preserves visible messages, plans and Unicode while omitting attachments, pending messages, internal/wiki-maintenance messages, tool arguments and private reasoning. Successful owned Codex and Claude compactions record timestamps; ignored compaction events do not. Markdown exports retain mailbox sender, question text and stable message/reply correlation IDs.

origin.problem: Context and export slash commands need provider compaction timestamps and a text-only conversation export.
origin.fix: Record successful compactions and export only visible messages/plans, with regression coverage.

tests.name: Local model lifecycle and context sizing
tests.covers: LM Studio, Ollama and llama.cpp router status, automatic load, unload, actual context limits, context growth, shared-provider serialization, cancellation, hosted-provider fallback and safe load failures. Existing conversations resume with the prepared context before sending. No live inference or downloaded model changes. Structured local inference uses schema-enabled chat completions, preserves runtime model IDs, images, usage and context growth/retry, rejects malformed/truncated responses, holds the provider lock through inference, respects Stop and leaves hosted inference unchanged. API providers run in Harness's own agent loop (no Codex): tool calls, approvals by access level, saved chat history, Stop; hosted structured calls use JSON mode.

origin.problem: LM Studio rejected a 16.5k prompt because the model was loaded with 8k context; Harness had no model load status or unload controls.
origin.fix: Discover supported native management APIs, coordinate local loads and forward the verified context to Codex, with explicit load/unload controls.

tests.name: Provider connection progress
tests.covers: Startup provider checks, overlapping requests, failures, and browser sign-in success, cancellation, browser-launch failure and disconnect all retain or clear transient progress correctly. No real provider calls.

origin.problem: Provider connection and browser sign-in had no shared progress indicator.
origin.fix: Expose transient per-provider connection state to the footer and Settings, retaining overlapping operations until completion.

tests.name: Hub chat and automatic delegation
tests.covers: Pinned chat model; Hub-only dynamic mid-tier selection using identical Jev/Smart policy and benchmark evidence across arbitrary Codex, Claude-only, Cursor-only and custom-provider models; measured capability extremes are excluded per model without bias from duplicate provider/effort rows, ties and sparse evidence retain usable choices, unknown measurements remain eligible, configurable effort is limited to Low/Medium while fixed/default-effort models stay eligible, pins persist without repeated routing and Auto/manual selection labels retain their origin, legacy pins are reselected, worker catalogs stay unchanged, manual choices work, invalid/high efforts and disabled/rate-limited candidates are rejected, Jev failure falls back to Smart and Stop discards late selections; tool-free inference for all providers, current chat access supplied separately from the planning sandbox, automatic worker creation with Auto and inherited access, attachments, result return through Hub pins despite stale queued/local composer models, persisted effective Hub mode, single Hub dispatch path avoiding manual pins including legacy previous-worker references, explicit worker selection retained, Jev/Smart review routing receives available Claude and local candidates with normal worker effort levels, follow-up reuse, responsive Hub during worker execution, protected identity, rejected escalation, invalid tools, late Stop results, persistent context summaries and retained history. Requested review workspace reaches the worker router; different workspaces require Full access, denied handoffs create nothing, and existing agents are not moved. Auto pins recover from disconnected providers, removed models and usage limits through the same eligible mid-tier policy; Claude-to-OpenAI switching preserves history, persists the replacement and reuses it. Manual pins are never silently replaced. LM Studio-only switching retains history, persists and reuses provider-default effort, skips classification for a sole eligible model, and rejects disabled/limited local models. Jev and Smart both accept fixed-effort candidates; local inference prepares the model and preserves its context configuration without inventing an effort level. Hub uses local structured inference instead of the Responses backend, and malformed replies cannot become agent actions. Typed Hub actions bind tool names to object arguments, preserve Windows/UNC paths, quotes, Unicode and pasted newlines without nested JSON parsing, remove optional nulls while retaining Auto and inherited permissions, and reject legacy strings, arrays, unknown fields, missing required values and invalid types/enums before side effects. Original Hub requests survive misleading notes, saved delegation, result delivery and intervening chat; exact original text drives routing and worker input. New requests reset prior task identity while same-request continuations retain it. Completion checks reject summaries instead of reviews, preserve original scope/images for bounded follow-ups, fail closed on malformed checks and cancelled/failed workers, and mark truncated requests/reports unverified without retries. Explicit batches create the full requested count at the chosen model/effort, queue all four Full-access workers in two bounded execution waves in the same workspace, persist and aggregate every result, reject invalid counts/full queues before side effects, and handle partial dispatch, cancellation and exhausted follow-up budgets without orphaned waits or false completion. Hub queues work for an explicitly selected busy bot with honest feedback, receives mailbox questions separately from completion reports, retains the correlated original request despite later chat, and answers without creating another assignment. Several agents are proposed once, created together on the next confirming message with an accurate created/failed count, and the list schema passes structured validation. Hub cannot delete agents. Dispatch persists direct versus review handling. Simple results bypass model selection, compaction and reply generation and reuse the saved report without duplicates, including when the Hub model is unavailable. Complex results combine assessment and reply in one call per returned assignment, including batch synthesis. Host build/test failures, worker failures, truncation, cancellation and bounded corrections remain enforced. Result returns skip optional reply suggestions; ordinary chats retain them. Empty final answers, including task-marker-only turns, cannot confirm a direct request complete. A Hub turn that fails or stops after the model decided drops its kept provider session, so the next turn rebuilds from the chat instead of continuing a decision that never ran.

origin.problem: The permanent agent mixed chat with execution and retained the task model.
origin.fix: Give Hub a pinned, isolated chat model and dispatch execution through existing agent controls.

tests.name: Worker routing difficulty and effort
tests.covers: Jev and Smart share one difficulty and task-kind contract. Difficulty alone controls effort independently of kind, risk, uncertainty, confidence or unrelated workspace signals. Routers only size the request and Harness picks the worker (pickPreset): Low/Medium keep an adequate current model, else the cheapest adequate measured worker (unscored workers unranked, unknown cost last); High/Xhigh choose the strongest measured model across all offered providers within the effort cap. Fixed-effort models, missing benchmarks, current-task continuity and stale sameTask flags remain covered. The four-prompt live evaluation fixture records misses and failures without dispatching workers. Structured inference validates full JSON and schema, retries malformed replies at most once, preserves usage, redacts model text from errors and honors Stop/limits without retrying. Main Bot uses an inactivity deadline: only active-provider text or reasoning extends it, silence still times out, late activity cannot resurrect timers, and ordinary routing keeps its fixed deadline. Cursor classifiers use private deny settings and cancel tool attempts before accepting a result; normal worker permissions and selected effort remain intact. These regressions are offline and use no paid calls.

origin.problem: Confidence alone promoted a bounded explanation to the strongest model while difficult concurrent queue repair stayed at Medium effort.
origin.fix: Classify task difficulty explicitly and share difficulty-based capability/effort selection across Jev and Smart without hardcoded models.

tests.name: Local Dark Light and System appearance
tests.covers: Appearance defaults to System before paint, restores valid choices, rejects corrupt saved values, persists changes locally, and remains usable when storage is unavailable. No provider or model is involved. The chosen appearance is reported to the desktop window so its launch background matches.

origin.problem: The app had only a hard-coded dark palette and no local appearance preference.
origin.fix: Use native light/dark CSS tokens with a validated pre-paint Dark/Light/System preference.

tests.name: Muse, Antigravity and DeepSeek Harness native CLI protocol and account boundaries
tests.covers: On Windows, Muse's installed version comes from .muse-version, never from its PowerShell launcher, which antivirus blocks (2026-10-27). Native discovery sends no inference, disabled accounts start no metadata or login process, native-only startup and routing work without Codex or an accidental Claude fallback. Public streaming excludes private reasoning. Resume retains session-bound MCP and explicit permissions; incompatible protocols, unsupported sandbox or continuation, missing usage, rejected approvals and cancellation fail honestly. Fixtures use the official ACP and Muse SDK protocols, with no paid calls. A native-only Gemini owner creates and delegates to a Muse execution context through real local MCP stdio processes and the ACP/MSP adapters. The simulated worker asks and receives an answer while active, retries deduplicate, final delivery has one owner, foreign-context helper calls fail, private thoughts stay hidden and all background slots release. No installed CLI or real-model inference runs. Synchronous Gemini process-creation failure removes its private policy directory and resets admission. Antigravity protocol fixtures cover native metadata, scoped helper credentials inherited outside project files, Full-access-only admission, text-only input, public streaming, generic call_mcp_tool events, explicit resume, unknown resumed usage, stopped startup, cancellation, changed-file preservation and linked-directory rejection. A Gemini owner also exchanges active-worker questions and one final result with an Antigravity execution context over real local MCP stdio. Gemini permission requests without rawInput are never remembered for the session; native muse/agy/gemini executables do not inherit ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE; a Muse stdin write error fails the turn instead of crashing. Gemini, Claude, Cursor and Muse send each image with the media type of its data URL. A confirmed Antigravity result survives unconfirmed cleanup, which still removes the generated worker file; a startup sweep removes only unchanged leftovers. Gemini's private system settings keep the administrator's settings and only turn off hooks, telemetry and subagents; a non-JSON admin file fails closed. The administrator's adminPolicyPaths are passed on after Harness's --admin-policy file, and Gemini is refused when system policy .toml files would make it ignore Harness's policy. A Gemini request without a tool name offers one-time approval only. DeepSeek Main keeps its private session after invalid JSON so the repair continues it without durable resume. DeepSeek and Muse refuse a resume that opens a different conversation, since resumed workers skip unchanged instructions. A self-updated Muse with a newer schema fingerprint still connects, while another schema version is refused without opening the Meta sign-in page; npm-installed dsh is found on any npm prefix on PATH and runs under Node rather than Harness's Electron, and a dsh that quits at start reports its own stderr reason.
tests.command: node --test tests/native-cli.test.cjs tests/muse.test.cjs tests/antigravity.test.cjs tests/deepseek.test.cjs tests/native-coordination.test.cjs && node --test --test-name-pattern="Allow for this session" tests/core.test.cjs && node --test --test-name-pattern="Update is offered" tests/providers-optional.test.cjs

origin.problem: Native adapters were absent, and native-only accounts could retain an unavailable Codex router or silently fall back to Claude.
origin.fix: Use native session protocols, explicit capability and permission checks, provider-specific dispatch, and deterministic protocol fixtures.

tests.name: Background window lifetime and update admission
tests.covers: Window close preserves the runner, draft and approval waits; reopen and second launch share one owner. Untrusted renderer IPC is rejected. Explicit Quit stays distinct. Autostart remains opt-in and uses matching source or packaged executable arguments. Updates wait for queued work, approval and cleanup; admission closes before install and reopens on known failure, while uncertain handoff keeps it closed. Unit checks plus an isolated Electron lifecycle smoke use no provider authentication, inference or login-item writes. Recovery verifies one-time original Hub/agent backups before reconciliation, preserves them on later launches and rejects bad backups or escaping agent ids. Deferred reviews and revision operations also block updates. Windows containment requires a private live-parent handshake before worker startup. Kernel jobs end normal detached child trees after runner crash, graceful quit, monitor failure or bounded control-lease loss; a fake installer survives outside the old runner job. Live checks use private fixtures and exact process identities. Installer fixture deletion requires confirmed process cleanup and bounded retries for delayed Windows file release. Invalid and missing handshakes cannot start work. Store-scoped lifetime jobs refuse an overlapping live owner without terminating it and fence prior descendant cleanup before admitting a replacement. Backups include validated registered execution stores. Update admission checks all actual controller connections and pending browser authentication; completed cached initialization promises do not block updates. Shared native/browser commands retain input validation and scoped Stop during asynchronous image preparation; closing or replacing its chat owner cannot admit a delayed message. Linux metadata fixtures reject mismatched service scope, identity or cleanup policy instead of claiming safe recovery. The headless server binds its port before the runner initializes, so a taken port submits no job. A desktop startup failure keeps the lifetime lease so its error window stays open. The Windows job name mixes in a private per-installation secret. A recovery backup is verified before it takes its name, so an interrupted copy cannot block later starts. Source installer shutdown uses a real second-instance handoff, waits for an owned worker to exit, ignores another installation, and never starts a runner for a shutdown-only launch.
tests.command: node --test tests/server.test.cjs tests/runner.test.cjs tests/runner-linux.test.cjs tests/runner-commands.test.cjs tests/runner-containment.test.cjs tests/updater.test.cjs && node tests/runner-live.cjs

origin.problem: Closing the window stopped all agents, and update checks ignored accepted queues and could admit a new writer while starting the installer.
origin.fix: Extract runner startup, keep the view detachable, preserve private IPC and single ownership, and guard update admission.

tests.name: Background quota reserve and safe limit waits
tests.covers: Valid saved allowance reports hold new background work at the configured threshold without consuming a submission attempt, while foreground chat remains usable. Tests cover malformed or unknown usage, reports beyond 100%, reset expiry, no invented reset, shared persistence, restart, threshold validation, cancellation during admission, a timer wake, and actual worker/router limit failures without cross-account failover. Owner tools expose paused state and reason. Remaining quota from unsupported providers stays unknown; active turns may finish. A hold without a reported reset is rechecked after 15 minutes, reading ChatGPT usage again, instead of waiting forever.
tests.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="quota|allowance limit|exhausted provider|background routing limit" tests/limits.test.cjs tests/agents.test.cjs

origin.problem: Background work could consume the last reported allowance or automatically switch accounts after a usage limit.
origin.fix: Persist supported allowance reports and hold background admission; retain uncertain limit failures for review without failover.

tests.name: Text/code attachments and retained snapshots
tests.covers: UTF-8 file snapshots preserve exact content and BOMs, reject malformed/binary inputs and path-like names, bound encoded bytes and attachment counts, and quote file contents as untrusted reference data. Controller and Hub tests retain snapshots through queues, metadata refresh, native history replacement and export without extending sandbox permissions. File-only requests get a useful default. Companion agents-ui checks cover selection, compact literal display, history recall and failed-send drafts. Companion document and dictation pools cover the additional inputs.

origin.problem: The composer accepted pasted images but could not attach immutable text/code files or retain their compact display through provider history replacement.
origin.fix: Add bounded UTF-8 snapshots, file chips, preserved display metadata and protected native-history retention.

tests.name: Saved artifact actions and tracked test processes
tests.covers: Bounded workspace publication rejects escapes, credential paths, links and oversized files. File fingerprints, stable task-scoped IDs, versioned replacement, rollback and active-turn checks preserve honest result evidence. Explicit Run rechecks the executable, rejects active writers and stale receipts, uses no shell or arguments and strips provider secrets from its environment. Open folder rejects replacement files. Tracked runs support independent Stop, failed cleanup retry, natural-exit cleanup and Quit; updates wait for them. Downloads freeze fingerprinted files or complete portable ZIP folders, preserve assets and executable modes, reject private/changed inputs and active writers, reserve disk capacity, cap concurrent transfers and release snapshots on Stop or restart. Uncertain cleanup blocks admission and updates. Native history preserves trusted receipts and rejects forged artifacts. Companion agents-ui checks verify literal paths, explicit ID-only actions and targeted test Stop. Fixtures never execute a game or prove a build.
